descriptive_title: Kindergarten Mathematics: Demonstrations — Collecting and Displaying Data (A8.1-A8.4)
subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.A8.1: sort objects or data using one attribute
curriculum_expectations.A8.2: collect and record data to answer questions of interest, and display it in concrete graphs or picture graphs
curriculum_expectations.A8.3: respond to data in concrete graphs and picture graphs by interpreting it and drawing conclusions
curriculum_expectations.A8.4: describe how likely familiar events are to happen

unit_overview: A 5-day Kindergarten unit on data demonstrations (A8.1-A8.4) framed around 'Data Detectives' — Detective Dot the Sorting Squirrel and Tally the Tally Cat. Day 1 categorises objects. Day 2 collects data by counting. Day 3 displays data on simple charts and pictographs. Day 4 reads and describes data. Day 5 closes with child-chosen data investigations. Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough.
unit_learning_goal: Children will categorise, count, display, and describe simple data.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Things can be sorted into groups by a SAME attribute — colour, shape, size.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can sort objects into groups.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Detective Dot sorts buttons by colour; children sort their own collections.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Counting things in groups gives us DATA — numbers we can use.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can collect data by counting things in groups.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children count classroom things by category and record.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We can DISPLAY data with pictures. Each picture stands for one thing counted.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can make a picture graph.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children build pictographs from their counts.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Some events ALWAYS happen, some SOMETIMES happen, some NEVER happen — that's LIKELIHOOD.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can tell if events ALWAYS, SOMETIMES, or NEVER happen.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children sort 6 events into ALWAYS / SOMETIMES / NEVER and write one event of their own.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We can be DATA DETECTIVES — sort, count, display, read.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can be a Data Detective for a question I pick.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children investigate a class question (favourite colour, snack, season); sort, count, graph, describe.

recurring_characters.name: Detective Dot the Sorting Squirrel
recurring_characters.role: Lead character. A friendly squirrel detective with magnifying glass who loves sorting acorns. Anchors all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A young squirrel in a deerstalker cap with a magnifying glass and acorn pouch. Bushy tail, alert ears, friendly grin.

recurring_characters.name: Tally the Tally Cat
recurring_characters.role: Detective Dot's partner. The 'count' character. Cameo Lessons 2-5.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A young cat with a tally chart and pencil. Stripes for tallies, eager smile.

threaded_vocabulary.child_friendly_definition: A group of things that are alike.
A picture that shows our data.

pedagogical_notes: Kindergarten data work is concrete — physical sorting and tallying.
Pictographs are appropriate; bar graphs come later.
Use class-wide questions to make data meaningful (favourite colour, snack).
Iterative process: sort → count → graph → describe.
canadian_context_notes: Class examples: favourite NHL team, favourite Tim Hortons donut, favourite season (extra fun in winter).
Sorting examples: snowflakes vs leaves vs raindrops, hockey sticks vs skates.
Real classroom data: lunch boxes by colour, shoes by type.
